findings.original: how this sophistication, peculiar to and characteristic of capitalist production, this complete inversion of the relation
findings.rewrite: how this falsification, peculiar to and characteristic of capitalist production, this complete inversion of the relation
findings.problem: "Falsification" implies a deliberate lie or forgery, whereas Marx means a real twisting or perversion of the relation (glossed by him as "complete inversion"), which the capitalists' minds then mirror.

notes_review: The logged calls are sound: Colbert for "Clobber" has only one reading, value-product and constant capital are rightly left to Marx's own definitions, and the Carlile sentence keeps "he imagines"/"he thinks" so the claim stays his. Only the "falsification" choice (note 11) overshoots: it adds a sense of deliberate deceit.
summary: Fidelity is very high: every figure, formula, law and citation survives, and the irony in p018-p019 and the footnotes is kept. Readability is good, though p002 is heavy with required first-use explanations.
